IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'redwood-runtime-prod' -> escalation policy 'infra-escalation'
PagerDuty: Alert  PD-74532: unhandled 5xx spike on /v1/generate (rate 12% over baseline) -> routed to 'infra-oncall'
Camille: ack — I'm seeing a page but I'm not on the infra rotation, this should hit api-team-oncall.
Owen: yep this looks like the escalation policy on the PD service was swapped earlier today during maintenance.
Nate: oh no. Was that the routing cleanup script? I ran a batch update around 07:10 UTC.
Leah: confirmed — the pd-service mapping changed from 'api-escalation' -> 'infra-escalation' in the recent deploy.
Camille: we need to stop paging the wrong people. Can someone set a temporary override and re-route the active alert?
Owen: on it. doing a temporary reroute via pd CLI. putting commands here:
```
# temporary override: route to api-team-oncall for 1h
pd incidents assign PD-74532 --assignee "Camille"
pd services update redwood-runtime-prod --escalation-policy api-escalation
```
Nate: I created a one-hour override in PD UI and re-pointed the service back to api-escalation. Confirmed active alert moved to Camille.
PagerDuty: Alert PD-74532 reassigned to Camille (api-team-oncall).
Camille: acknowledged. digging into errors now — logs show a noisy downstream cache (kv-fetch) failing with timeouts that surface as 502s.
Leah: can we mute further pages until we have mitigation? We should avoid waking infra people for api issues.
Owen: muted the service paging channel for infra-escalation (policy-level mute) and set a suppression rule for duplicate bursts.
Nate: mitigation plan: 1) temporary traffic shift to warm pool (traffic split 20%->warm), 2) scale up api pool by 2 nodes, 3) investigate kv cache timeouts and fallback logic. I'm kicking off scale now.
Camille: live metrics: 5xx rate peaked at 17% 5m ago, now down to 8% after first traffic shift. Affected customers: 14 requests/min failing, mostly low-volume tenants. No billing impacts reported yet.
Support Team: notifying Tier 2 support and flagging impacted customers in Zendesk. Will assemble a short customer note if degradation persists.
Leah: for post-incident we need to revert the accidental escalation-policy change from the deploy pipeline. Add rollback to the PR that modified pd mappings and add an automated test to validate mapping owner.
Owen: opened PR #2345 to enforce that. Also adding a step to the deploy job to run `pd services get` after changes and fail on mismatches.
IncidentBot: Note: PagerDuty override in place until 1 hour from 1768200450 (will auto-expire).
PagerDuty: Escalation policy 'infra-escalation' was unintentionally set on service 'redwood-runtime-prod' by deploy-bot at 1768199400 — change reverted.
Camille: ok 5xx back to ~2% now, scaling helped. I think we can keep the override until tomorrow morning to be safe, then remove once automated tests are in.
Nate: leaving override extended +1h. I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft.
Leah: action items:
- Owen: ship PR that blocks wrong PD mapping in pipeline (PR #2345)
- Nate: postmortem draft + timeline
- Camille: logs and root-cause on kv timeouts; confirm if cache client update rolled out recently
- Support Team: customer notification draft if needed
Camille: thanks everyone. tagging for handoff to next oncall — @Owen you're next for follow-up.
Owen: got it. I'll watch overnight and follow up in the morning with RCA notes. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Thread closed by Camille (ack + mitigation underway). Remember to file an incident ticket (INC-2026-187) with the timeline.
